title: Manager-led rapid onboarding + interview debrief kit
content:
Purpose:
Quick, manager-focused kit to run pre-hire orientation, run interview debriefs consistently, and land a 14-day rapid onboarding for ICs. Intended for hiring managers and people-ops partners who want a lightweight flow they can run without waiting on a full ops playbook.

Who this helps:
- First-time managers hiring at Redwood
- Managers needing a compact debrief rubric for cross-functional panels
- People-ops partners who will QA offers and first-14-day plans

High-level goals:
- Reduce time-to-impact for new hires (target: first meaningful PR within 14 days)
- Make post-interview debriefs fast and consistent (<= 10 minutes per candidate)
- Standardize manager responsibilities during first 14 days so ops can scale support

Notes-to-self / approach:
- This is intentionally terse: prioritize checkboxes and copy-paste templates managers can use in Slack/Email.
- Keep debrief rubric anchored to skills + risk signals (culture fit, execution, hiring bar). Avoid long narrative.
- Add a short escalation flow for red flags (security, data access, behavioral).

Pre-hire checklist (manager) — do before verbal offer:
[ ] Confirm role scope with hiring partner (1-paragraph summary + 3 success signals)
[ ] Create a 14-day impact plan (see template below) and share with people-ops
[ ] Identify primary buddy (not the manager) and invite them to onboarding planning 
[ ] Book 30/60/90 check-ins on calendar — put in candidate offer packet as "onboarding cadence"
[ ] Slack intro template ready (one-liner + 3 links)

Interview debrief rubric (5 min panel-ready):
Scoring: 1 = fail, 2 = below bar, 3 = meets bar, 4 = strong, 5 = outstanding
Categories (score each 1-5) + 1-line evidence:
- Technical craft / problem solving: 
  - Evidence to record: code sample, design trade-offs, time-to-solution, ownership examples
- Product sense / user empathy:
  - Evidence: tradeoffs, prioritization examples, user impact metrics referenced
- Communication & collaboration:
  - Evidence: clarity, cross-team examples, acceptance of feedback
- Culture & values alignment (Redwood norms):
  - Evidence: reciprocity, bias for action, operational rigor examples
- Risk signals (binary notes):
  - Security/infra complacency? [yes/no], poor ownership history? [yes/no]

Decision guidance (after scoring):
- If avg >= 3.7 and no risk signals -> proceed to verbal offer
- If 3.0 <= avg < 3.7 -> ask for follow-up task or second-stage interview (focus on gap area)
- If avg < 3.0 or any high risk signal -> decline and capture reasons in 1-2 lines

Debrief template (copyable Slack/PR template):
Candidate: {Name} (role: {role})
Panel: {names}
Scores: craft {x}, product {x}, comms {x}, values {x} -> avg {x.xx}
Top evidence (2 bullets):
- 
- 
Risks / unknowns (1-2 lines):
Recommendation: {hire / no-hire / follow-up task} + next step owner
Link to candidate packet: {Confluence / GH gist}

14-day rapid onboarding template (manager-owned):
Goal: first meaningful contribution (bugfix, infra change, small feature) + connect with core collaborators
Day 0 (before start):
- Offer packet sent (welcome note, first-day agenda, laptop & software checklist, security readouts) — owner: people-ops
- Manager: send Slack intro message and calendar invites for week 1

Week 1 (Day 1-5):
Day 1:
- 9:00-9:30 welcome + company values quick intro (manager)
- 10:00-11:00 team orientation + org map (manager)
- 11:30 meet buddy, set up dev environment checklist (buddy)
- 2:00 access walk-through (SRE/IT) — confirm access to repos, infra, tickets
Day 2-3:
- Pair on a small task with buddy (goal: complete CI PR)
- 1:1 with product partner to review roadmap and first 14-day impact plan
Day 4-5:
- Manager-run brown bag: "how we ship" (release process, rollbacks, postmortems)
- Deliver first micro-PR + review loop (aim for merged by EOD Fri)

Week 2 (Day 6-14):
- Handoff larger micro-feature / bug (owner: manager)
- Meet 1:1 with 3 cross-functional partners (SRE, Product, Design)
- End-of-week 2 review: manager gives consolidated feedback and updates 30/60/90 plan

Checklist snippets managers can paste into a ticket:
- "New hire environment readiness: repo access, infra tokens, Slack channels (done by IT/SRE)"
- "First PR target: small bugfix with CI + test coverage (owner: new hire + buddy)"

Common risk triggers (escalate to people-ops):
- Repeated access failures after day 2 (possible permissions or identity issue)
- Team culture mismatch reported by multiple collaborators
- Security or PII exposure during early tasks

Templates (copy/paste)
Slack intro (manager):
"Everyone — please welcome {Name}, joining as {role} on {team}. They’ll be pairing with {buddy} this week. Quick FYI: their first impact target is {one-sentence}. Welcome!"

Offer verbal note (manager to candidate):
"Hi {Name}, excited to extend an offer for {role} at Redwood. We plan a start date of {date}. Onboarding will include a 14-day impact plan and a dedicated buddy. People-ops will send the official packet by EOD. I'll follow up with next steps — congrats!"

Manager debrief quick checklist (post hire):
[ ] Confirm team calendar invites are in new hire's calendar
[ ] Share 14-day impact plan and acceptance confirmation with people-ops
[ ] Confirm buddy has allocated 4 hours/week for pairing during first 2 weeks
[ ] Create first micro-PR ticket and assign to new hire

Unresolved questions / TODOs in this doc:
- Should we require managers to run a live 10-min calibration with people-ops for hires above L4? (pros: quality control; cons: slowdowns)
- Can we auto-generate the 14-day checklist from offer acceptance to reduce ops work? (ticket: HR-4412)

References / links to deeper resources:
- Manager onboarding templates (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PE/manager-onboard-templates
- Interview rubric canonical (people-ops): HR-3319
- Security onboarding checklist: SRE-bootcamp repo PR #76

Quick retrospective notes from pilot (Sept-Oct 2025):
- Most managers appreciated the one-page debrief; reduced time to offer by ~18% in pilot groups
- Common miss: managers forgot to reserve buddy time — add explicit calendar invite step

If you use this doc, please leave a short note at bottom with: 
- name, team, what you changed, and date.

END
